feasible.reason: The proposal addresses exactly the stated threat (no FI regression net) and every repo_evidence claim checks out: ci.yml has no rainbow step; nightly.yml's checkct job is workflow_dispatch-only (line 8) AND continue-on-error (line 169), so even that is not gating; tools/sca/fi_target FAILS TO BUILD today against current fi.rs (E0425: crate::rng::byte_nonsecret missing — the harness rng stub still exports byte()); c10_sign_target signs with plain sk.sign (main.rs:105/107) while production crypto.rs:350/358 uses sign_with_shuffle with two independent seeds; check_fi_ir.sh covers only pqsigner_fi::fi_min via a scratch-crate IR probe and is absent from invariant-gates (Makefile:4445-4460); all nine cited issues are OPEN; docs/STATUS.md:421 records the sweep campaign as 'only smoke-run'. It is a pure host-side process change — no hardware dependency, so kind=process is correct. The ELF-level gate (item 4) is realisable: fi.rs primitives are #[inline(never)] and nm on target/pqsigner-release/secure.elf shows 137 surviving pqsigner_fi::check_true_into_sentinel::<…> monomorphisations to anchor on. Cost M / priority P1 are defensible for a regression net that is cheaper than silicon FI; the proposal already flags the two real limits (emulation fidelity, baseline gaming). Corrections below are material to how the gate must be specified, not to whether it defends.
feasible.corrections: (1) Baseline must be keyed on (symbol, DWARF source line), never on rainbow's absolute instruction index: c10_sign_full_sweep.py:246-268 already pins checkpoints to the binary hash because any code change shifts every position, so an index-keyed baseline would churn on every commit and be useless as a diff. (2) 'Full C10 sweep' is a SPARSE SAMPLE, not an exhaustive map: the script estimates ~73 s/fault at a 500,000-instruction stride over a ~1.12 B-instruction sign (≈2,240 positions × 3 models ≈ 136 CPU-h; /8 workers ≈ 17 h). An exhaustive single-skip sweep of sign is ~2.6 k years in Unicorn — the published SECURE/INSECURE map must state its stride/coverage fraction, and a weekly 'full' run is still a sample. Exhaustive sweeps are feasible only for the small gates (fi.rs, confirm/chord, staging state machine, fsbl compare/branch — with stride on the hash body). (3) Item (3)'s pass criterion is wrong as written: the F-16 shuffle (sphincs-c10/src/shuffle.rs) permutes only WOTS-chain and FORS-tree order; the message hash, R, FORS index derivation and layer-root computations are unshuffled, so a same-hash-call-index fault in those regions corrupts both passes identically even with DISTINCT seeds and ct_eq is structurally blind there. The gate must assert forge-release == 0 overall and classify which gate (ct_eq vs verify-before-release) caught each fault — expect a residual class that only verify catches, which is precisely #593's SHAFI question; do not encode 'ct_eq catches iff seeds differ' as the assertion. Implementing 'hash-call index' needs a rainbow function hook with a counter on the SHA-256 compress entry, not the stock instruction-index fault models. (4) Emulation fidelity gap specific to pq1: rainbow sweeps the software sha2 path, whereas pq1 signs through the STM32 HASH peripheral (hw-sha256 extern hooks) — HASH DIN/DOUT/DMA faults and clock-glitch effects on the peripheral are unmodelled; say so in the receipt rather than citing Ledger's generic caveat. (5) The ELF gate must run on the dual-se stm32u585 image that `make release` actually produces, not target/pqsigner-release/secure.elf as built today (that one links MockSecureElement); a true mode-production+optiga ELF cannot be built while the OPTIGA_S2_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED fence holds, so the gate has to be re-run on the final profile once S-2 closes (LTO decisions can differ per feature set). Prefer per-primitive structural patterns (≥2 `bl` to the closure + sentinel `cmp` inside each check_true_into_sentinel::<…> instance, as README.md:66-72 already does by hand) over per-site absolute load/compare counts, which will churn with every call-site edit. (6) Step zero is unlisted: repair the fi_target rng stub (byte_nonsecret(u8) + AtomicU8 contract) and port c10_sign_target to sign_with_shuffle with harness-supplied seeds; until then `make -C tools/sca fi` cannot even run. (7) Self-hosted runner infrastructure does not exist anywhere in the repo (every job is ubuntu-latest, whose 6 h cap rules out even the per-night subset) — that ops cost is outside 'M' and should be stated; (8) nightly.yml's checkct precedent is itself non-gating (workflow_dispatch + continue-on-error), so the new job must be scheduled and blocking or it repeats that pattern.
